oneLine: Bitcoin and Ethereum gained 0.76% and 0.85% as the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 0.25% in its first hike since July 2023.
caveman: Here's what happened on September 16: The Federal Reserve, which is like the bank that runs money in the United States, said it would make borrowing money more expensive by raising interest rates—that usually makes people worried about the economy. But traders who buy and sell Bitcoin and Ethereum didn't panic. Bitcoin went up 0.76% and Ethereum went up 0.85%, which is a small but positive move. Some smaller coins had huge single-day swings (like one coin called ONE jumped 55.8%), but we can't figure out why from public news. The day was generally calm for big coins even though an important economic announcement happened.
priceVolumeSummary: All five major venues (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, Gate) quoted virtually identical prices for Bitcoin and Ethereum—within $30–50 per coin—showing traders agreed on fair value. Binance dominated volume, trading $11.8 billion in BTC futures and $10.6 billion in ETH futures, with the other four venues combined handling roughly similar size.
positioningSummary: Traders were decidedly bullish. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio was 1.53 on Binance, meaning over 1.5 traders bet on up for every 1 betting down; Ethereum's was even more skewed at 3.2 to 1. Funding rates (the daily cost to hold leveraged positions) stayed positive across all venues, ranging from 2.5% to nearly 11% annually, indicating sustained bullish positioning. Open interest was mixed: Bybit saw 1.25% decline while Binance grew 1.16%, suggesting some traders closed longs but new money entered elsewhere.
stocksSummary: Asian stock markets climbed during their morning sessions (which closed before the Fed announcement): South Korean semiconductor stocks led (SK Hynix +3.7%, Samsung +4.1%), Hong Kong AI stocks surged (MiniMax +9.6%, Zhipu AI +5.2%), and Chinese robotics rallied (Unitree Robotics +8.9%). Commodity futures also gained: gold +1.78%, silver +3.38%, copper +2.89%, while oil slipped −0.91%. These moves likely reflected pre-Fed positioning as traders hedged before the rate decision.

topThree.headline: Federal Reserve raises interest rates 0.25% to 3.75%–4.00%, first hike since July 2023
topThree.what: The US Federal Reserve voted to increase its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points (25 basis points) to a range of 3.75%–4.00%. This is the first rate increase in over three years. Fed officials signaled that more increases may come, though they may slow the pace. A rate hike typically increases borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, which can reduce economic activity.

glossary.definition: One-hundredth of a percent (0.01%). Used to describe small changes in interest rates or percentages. A 0.25% rate increase equals 25 basis points.
The first and largest cryptocurrency by market value. It is a digital currency that runs on a network of computers and records transactions on a public ledger called blockchain.
A blockchain network and its associated cryptocurrency. It enables programmable applications and smart contracts on top of a public ledger, similar to Bitcoin but more flexible.
A fund that tracks the price of an asset (like Bitcoin or gold) and trades on regular stock exchanges. Investors can buy and sell ETF shares like stocks.

A fee that traders with leveraged positions pay to each other every few hours (often 8 hours on crypto exchanges). When funding rates are positive, traders betting on price increases pay those betting on decreases. High positive rates signal bullish sentiment; high negative rates signal bearish sentiment.

A bet placed with borrowed money, allowing a trader to control a larger amount than they deposited. For example, 10x leverage means controlling $10,000 worth of Bitcoin while depositing only $1,000. Leverage amplifies both gains and losses.

A comparison of how many traders are betting on price increases (long) versus price decreases (short). A ratio of 1.53 means 1.53 traders are long for every 1 trader short. Higher ratios indicate bullish sentiment.

The current fair-value price of a futures contract, calculated by exchanges using the spot price plus a funding adjustment. It is used to decide if a leveraged position should be forcibly closed (liquidated).

The total number of leveraged positions (long and short bets combined) currently open on an exchange. Rising open interest suggests new money entering; falling open interest suggests traders closing positions.
A crypto exchange or trading platform where futures contracts are bought and sold. In this report, venues include Binance, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, and Gate.
